title: Non-experts’ trust in XAI is unreasonably high
core_idea: Investigate whether explainable AI (using SHAP-like explanations) actually enables non-expert users to detect and challenge biased or flawed AI decisions by studying trust in a real-world high-risk scenario (academic grading). The study conducts an experiment with 63 non-expert participants who believed an AI graded their exams, with an experimental manipulation simulating biased lower grades, to probe how explainability affects users' ability to critically engage with AI decisions.
tldr: The study aims to assess if XAI explanations help non-experts identify and contest biased AI decisions by running an experiment using SHAP-like explanations in a simulated academic grading context with 63 participants.
